title: syslog Logging driver support
body:
### Feature request description

I would like to request adding a syslog Logging driver, as Docker has.
It would allow using logs seamlessly on resources constrained environments which do not use journald, as OpenWrt.

Related:
#12537

comments.body: This sounds like a good idea. What do others think? @containers/podman-maintainers
We've been tracking this for a while, but in Jira not Github, so it's good to have a tracking issue for this. This is definitely on the roadmap now that we have Conmon v3.
Hi, Is this something I can pick up?
@hsaokar are you aware of whats going on with conmon v3 and podman's dependency of it ?

At a very high level, yes, but not in details (yet). 
My understanding is 1) the real change has to happen in conmon and then gets plumbed thru into  containers/common and podmon 2) conmon v3 is set to replace conmon, so it is desirable to add this support in v3 instead.
A friendly reminder that this issue had no activity for 30 days.
That would be really nice to have. There are several hardened Linux distributions that eschew systemd.

Hi, I'd like to take on Docker-compatible `--log-driver syslog` for this issue.

I've looked at Conmonv3.md and conmon-v3: there's already local syslog via `--log-path syslog`, but Podman doesn't accept `--log-driver syslog` yet, and the full Docker option set (syslog-address, facility, format, tag, TLS, …) isn't wired through. I plan to work on the conmon-v3 + Podman path unless maintainers want v2 instead.

Aiming for Docker parity on names and behavior so existing configs mostly work. I'd do Podman validation/API first and extend conmon-v3 where needed; small PRs rather than one big dump.

For `podman logs`, I'd begin with forward-only + a clear error, and treat dual logging as a second step unless you want it upfront.

More design detail in a follow-up here; I'll start coding in ~a week if no major objections.

#12537

For this, I think we need a way of identifying which log drivers our Conmon supports - perhaps a flag in there - so we can tell if we're talking to a Conmon v3 that supports syslog and other things, or a legacy Conmon without it.

Yeah, that makes sense. I had the same concern. Right now Podman already shells out to `conmon --version` for info, but that doesn't tell you which log drivers the binary actually supports, so we'd be guessing if we only look at the path or a v3 vs v2 version string.

I'm happy to include an explicit capability check in the design. Something like a conmon flag that lists supported log drivers (or a structured `--version`/features output Podman can parse once at startup or cache), and then reject `--log-driver syslog` at create time when the configured conmon doesn't advertise it, instead of failing obscurely when the container starts.

If you have a preference for the flag shape (dedicated `--log-drivers` vs extending `--version` vs JSON features blob), I'll align with that in the first conmon-v3 / Podman PR that touches this.

In general I am somwhat unhappy with feature checks that require us to execute another binary first, that means that each container create would get the overheard of an extra exec call which seems unnecessary in 99% of the cases.

Why would it not be good enough to pass that to the normal conmon command when we launch the container and then it fails? We just need to make sure the error returned by it is reasonable.

In any case regarding conmon features/design make sure to include @jankaluza and @simek-m, they might be working on this already

I think the combination makes sense. And if Podman only runs `conmon --version` when someone actually asks for a v3-only thing like `--log-driver syslog`, normal creates don't pay for the extra exec at all, which I think covers @Luap99 's concern. It also means we can fail at create time with "this needs conmon v3" instead of failing later at start.

I like the `--log-plugin` idea too. Apart from avoiding the v2 `./syslog` file problem, it gives us an obvious place to pass driver options, something like `--log-plugin syslog --log-plugin-opt syslog-address=tcp://...`, instead of adding a new top-level flag for each option.

For what it's worth, the part people seem to need most is remote delivery, not the local socket. Harbor for example sends all its services to `syslog-address: tcp://localhost:1514` (goharbor/harbor#23881), so address, facility and format support is what would unblock it.

Once the flag shape is agreed I can pick up the Podman side (option validation, the v3 check, inspect/API, docs and tests), and help with the conmon-v3 part too if that's useful to @jankaluza and @simek-m.
Let's see if others in a discussion have an opinion, but I like the --log-plugin and --log-plugin-opt as new conmon-v3 options. I can implement the conmon-v3 part once we agree on a option.

> The syslog is actually good example, because the conmon-v2 treats --log-path syslog as an instruction to log to file ./syslog and simply continues, so the conmon-v2 would not fail. Thinking about it, this behavior is somehow unfortunate. Maybe we should switch to different flag in v3 altogether, something like --log-plugin and let the --log-path to be backwards compatible with conmon-v2, but add new plugins support only to --log-plugin.

Oh my yes that was broken design in the old conmon, we should absolutely have a dedicated option to set the log driver. `--log-plugin` works though I would prefer `--log-driver` to keep the name of the option the same as we have on podman already.
I agree with you to only support new driver on a new option and keep the old behavior as is for backwards compat.
Cool, I will use `--log-driver` and prepare conmon-v3 PR.
This SGTM, let's correct the design when we can.

One dropped me a link in https://github.com/goharbor/harbor/pull/23881 to here ....

@mheon Can you confirm that we will **NOT** or mostlikely  **NOT** see this feature in RHEL 10? That will help me a lot.

Thanks, `--log-driver` works for me.

@jankaluza before you open the conmon-v3 PR: are you planning to use `--log-driver-opt` (or similar) for things like `syslog-address`? I'll mirror whatever you pick on the Podman side.

Also, is that PR mostly the new option and wiring, or does it include the network syslog side too (tcp/udp address, facility, format)? Either way is fine — I just want to avoid stepping on the same code.

I'll start on Podman: accept `--log-driver syslog`, validate the log opts, the v3-only check when syslog is requested, and inspect/API. I can open a draft once I have something reviewable.

@zadnarock , I will go with `--log-driver` and `--log-driver-opt` - I have WIP PR here https://github.com/containers/conmon-v3/pull/66. I also have to fork conmon-v2 tests into conmon-v3 in order to fix tests (that's https://github.com/containers/conmon-v3/pull/67). Now I will work on remote syslog, but I think I won't finish that today - I'll see.
